blocks.text: Monoclonal antibodies are central to personalised medicine, allowing treatment tailored to individual patients. Continued innovation in their design and production is needed to make therapies more effective and better suited to each patient's biology.

blocks.caption: Advantages of monoclonal antibodies (book's list)
rows: compared with traditional drugs, with potential for long-lasting effects
each binds a single target with little variability
the book describes them as easy to prepare for research
lower risk of interactions with other medicines

blocks.text: The book adds that modern technologies allow thousands of potential antibodies to be tested at the same time, shortening development and allowing faster responses to urgent problems such as infectious diseases and cancer.

blocks.prompt: Why do monoclonal antibodies cause less damage to healthy tissue in cancer treatment?
blocks.explanation: They bind only to their specific target antigen on the cancer cells, unlike conventional chemotherapy, which also harms normal dividing cells.

items: Advantages: low toxicity, few side effects, high specificity, targeted cancer therapy, research use, fewer drug interactions.
